title: Model transition playlist - Tobias
content:
Notes to self: a compact, informal plan for a gradual model transition that avoids classic canary noise and focuses on controlled cohort choreography. The term 'playlist' is because this will be a sequence of short, repeatable steps (tracks) we can play and rewind if needed.

Objective:
- Promote model v2025-11b into hosted pool with minimal user-visible regressions and predictable cost delta.
- Keep per-token cost increase under 12% during steady state.
- Ensure rollback path is < 10 minutes for high-severity signals.

Key constraints / background:
- New model has ~8% higher avg token cost, ~5% better log-likelihood on eval set, and inconsistent latency tail in region eu-west-1 under large-sequence requests.
- Dedicated customers pinned to v2025-09c must not be affected.
- KV-cache layout slightly changed; cold-starts will be more expensive until warm.
- Telemetry (token breakdown) is available per-request but sampled at 1/100 for embeddings-heavy routes.

High-level sequence (playlist tracks):
1) Silent shadowing (track 1) - 24h
   - Route 0% traffic to new model but mirror 100% of requests asynchronously (no client response).
   - Purpose: capture real request shapes, sequence lengths, function-calling patterns, and worst-case prompts.
   - Output: cache-warm heatmap, histograms of sequence lengths, top 20 prompt prefixes.

2) Micro-bundle probe (track 2) - 6h repeated twice across two quiet windows
   - Allocate tiny cohort (0.05% traffic) routed live to new model. 1-in-20 requests are promoted for live response.
   - Enforce strict safety and latency guards: if p95 latency > baseline + 350ms OR error rate > baseline * 2 -> immediate rollback of this track.
   - Compare token economics per-request using tokenizer parity check (to rule out tokenization mismatch accounting).

3) Client-sparse progressive (track 3) - 3 days
   - Identify 150 low-risk clients (low variance, internal customers, or opt-in pilot). Assign them to cohort groups of 10-20 clients.
   - Stagger group starts by 3 hours to observe cross-client propagation (cache priming).
   - Pin specific clients to new model at TCP edge (client-level pin in routing table) to avoid global split churn.

4) Prefix warming sweep (track 4) - concurrent with track 3
   - Use synthetic requests derived from top 20 prefixes from shadowing to prime KV cache on new nodes in each region.
   - Warm-up cadence: 10k synthetic tokens per prefix across region; avoid saturating autoscaler by throttling to 30qps per replica.

5) Flow fraction lift (track 5) - 48–72h ramp
   - Move from pinned clients to a weighted split: 1% -> 3% -> 7% -> 15% over 48–72h depending on telemetry.
   - Use model-agnostic sampling to ensure diverse latencies (not only short completions).

6) Broad soak + economics check (track 6) - 7 days
   - If metrics are stable, increase to target: 25% live traffic for 7 days, then evaluate.
   - Run cost/quality regression: per-route average cost, perplexity on held-out prompts, and human-eval spot checks (10k samples randomized).

7) Full flip (track 7) - gating criteria only
   - Criteria: stable latency tails (p95 within +200ms), error rate delta < 0.5ppt, quality regressions < 1% on evals, cost delta acceptable to biz (<=12%).
   - If pass, plan a single downtime-free flip with DNS/routing change and final cache priming run.

Safety windows / gates (always watch):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per region; immediate abort if p95 increases > 350ms for 10m sliding window.
- Errors: 5xx spike or model-specific exceptions -> pause rollout and capture request dump.
- Quality: automatic hitbands on key QA prompts (we have 3 golden prompts per core route). Fail if >2% regression in any route over 1h.
- Customer complaints: if 3 unique customers open P1s referencing hallucination/incorrect outputs within a 60m window, pause promotion.

Rollback primitives (fastest to slowest):
- Track abort: stop current ramp and revert weighted routing to previous fraction.
- Pin back: re-pin affected clients to previous version via routing API (instant).
- Node drain and replace: scale down new-model replicas to 0 in a region if local problem.
- Opt-out patch: short runtime kill-switch toggled via control plane for problematic model binary.

Operational checklist (commands & notes):
- Before any live traffic: create a roll-id in the release tracker and a temporary Slack channel #roll-tobias-<id>.
- Run housekeeping: confirm autoscaler policies for new model flavor, ensure circuit-breaker thresholds are set (latency and error).
- Preflight queries: run 1000 sampled preflight requests across EU/US/APAC and save token profiles to /tmp/roll-<id>-profiles.json.
- Telemetry: enable higher-frequency sampling (1/10) for p95 windows during the first 24h of each track.
- Throttle knobs: set max qps per replica to 60 for first 48h.

Telemetry dashboard slices to watch (custom quick checks):
- Per-route: mean tokens/req, mean cost/req, p95 latency, 5xx rate, top N prefixes causing outliers.
- Cross-tenant: sigma of latency across tenants, top 5 tenants by delta.
- Cache health: cold-hit ratio, average KV load latencies, bytes-in-cache per replica.
- Quality: golden-prompt correctness rate (binary), perplexity delta on eval bucket, manual spot check list.

Questions / uncertainties to resolve before broad lift:
- Is there a safe way to transfer warmed KV snapshots from shadow nodes to live replicas without exposing internal keys? (security + cost)
- Should we use a model-variant fallback vs full replacement for short tails? Fallbacks reduce churn but complicate routing logic.
- How will deduped logs affect human-eval sampling; need clean sampling pipeline.

Post-roll actions:
- 24h post: synthesize anomalies and share TL;DR to #serving-runtime and product.
- 72h post: run cost analysis and finalize billing note for finance.
- 7 days post: write short postmortem w/ metrics and lessons; capture what synthetic prefixes helped most.

Quick command cheatsheet (examples):
- pin client: rwctl routing pin --client <id> --model v2025-11b --region eu-west-1
- change weight: rwctl routing weight --model v2025-11b --weight 3
- rollback model globally: rwctl routing set-default --model "v2025-09c"

Loose end todo (short):
- [ ] confirm telemetry sampling increase won't blow monitoring retention budget
- [ ] mock a partial cache-eviction scenario in staging
- [ ] add new golden-prompts for Spanish and French routes
- [ ] coordinate with CS: identify 10 customers willing to be pilot testers

Random notes/heuristics to remember:
- Tiny pinned cohorts often reveal cache-priming correlation that a pure weighted split misses.
- Synthetic prefix warming is surprisingly effective at reducing cold-start token cost but watch rate-limiting on autoscaler.
- Keep manual spot-checking timeboxed (max 60m per day) during initial ramp to avoid bias.

End of playlist. Revisit after track 3 or earlier if smoke.

-- Tobias
(updated 2026-02-03)
